draft.title: Five-number summary and box plots
card: The five-number summary lists five values in order: the minimum, Q1, the median, Q3 and the maximum. Together they show where the data starts, centres and ends.
A box plot draws these five values above a number line. The box runs from Q1 to Q3, a line inside the box marks the median, and whiskers reach out to the minimum and the maximum.
Example: 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13, 15. The median is 9. Q1 is the middle of the lower half, 6, and Q3 is the middle of the upper half, 13. The summary is 4, 6, 9, 13, 15.
The plot has four sections: the left whisker, the two parts of the box and the right whisker. Each holds about a quarter of the values, so a longer section means those values are more spread out.

3.alt: A box plot for the data 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13, 15. The left whisker starts at 4, the box runs from 6 to 13 with the median line at 9, and the right whisker ends at 15.

draft.remember: A box plot is the five-number summary drawn on a number line: whiskers to the minimum and maximum, a box from Q1 to Q3, and a median line.

a.q: The box plot shows time spent on homework in minutes. What value is at the right end of the box?
a.why: The box runs from Q1 to Q3, so its right end is Q3, which is 60. The 90 is the right end of the whisker, which marks the maximum, not the box.
a.clue: The box ends at the quartiles, not at the maximum.

fig.alt: A box plot of homework time in minutes. The left whisker starts at 10, the box runs from 30 to 60 with the median line at 40, and the right whisker ends at 90.

b.q: Ravi's quiz scores have the five-number summary 4, 11, 14, 17, 20. In his box plot, which two values are the ends of the left whisker?
b.why: The left whisker runs from the minimum, 4, to Q1, 11. The values 11 and 14 are the ends of the left part of the box, which is a different section.
b.clue: The whisker joins the minimum to the start of the box.
